utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the witness is still being examined.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the photograph from Exhibit 18, 7375.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us what we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7375, you find the bridge on -- in Brod which is outside the Foca town centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why did you document this bridge when you were in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to witnesses, they allege that Muslim captured men were lined on the bridge, and they were shot and killed, and the bodies were thrown over the bridge, and the bodies were later seen floating down the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you recall from which place these men came from and when that happened?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall from which place they came from, but it happened in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Okay. And did you find when you were on this bridge in Foca in 1996, did you find indication for this massacre?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found indication, indentured [sic] marks or bullet holes, we would call it, on the right-hand side of the fence of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, we would like to put these photos to the witness. The next photos will be the photos 7383, 7384, and 7385.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, can you show us on those photos such impacts?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, these were some kind of indentured [sic] marks or bullet holes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the third photo? Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing out some quite visible impacts on these photos from the railing of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in the photo binders you have also a chapter that is called "Ribarski Dom."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And with the help of the usher, would you please show the witness the photo 7408 -- no, 09, 09, 7411, and 7413.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. What building, what kind of building is on this photo 7409?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is called the Ribarski Dom. It was a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And what was significant about the restaurant that you found it worth making photos of?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to witnesses, they alleged that the Serb politicians held a meeting at this building, and also the Serb military gathered there from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And can we now have the other two photos, 7411 and 7413. What do we see here? What is it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to 710 or 711?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Eleven.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a front view of the Ribarski Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The entrance?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entrance.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And the next one, 7413, what does it show?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The side view facing the river, and the Brena Block of flats.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you -- in the photo binder, I would like to have put in front of you photo 7360 and also 7364, and if you please tell us what it shows. First this, yes, that's the photo 7360.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7360 is the entrance to the Brioni farm. And did you want 7361?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, 64, 64. It's on the other sheet. What do we --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7364 is the housing quarters where prisoners were kept during lunch breaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the farm, why did you make photos of the farm?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prisoners were taken there for work details from KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. That's enough. You made quite a lot of photos from the KP Dom itself. Where was it situated?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: KP Dom was situated in Donje Polje, on the east bank of the River Drina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in the neighbourhood of the KP Dom, did you notice any damaged buildings?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were several houses that were damaged, a mosque, and the bridge opposite the KP Dom was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Had you -- had your visit to the prison been announced to the local authorities before you went there?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did announce our visit more or less two or three weeks prior to our going there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was it made clear to the authorities in Foca that you wanted to inspect and photograph the prison and see all the rooms?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was made very clear to the authorities in a written request that certain detention rooms and prison cells were to be viewed by us, and the -- we required assistance from the prison officials, and to speak to certain officials related to the KP Dom, and to make photos and take measurements of certain detention rooms and prison cells.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how many days did you actually work in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was two days.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I will take care of this.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was two days, the 17th and the 18th. The 18th included the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who received you when you arrived in the prison?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zoran Sekulovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He introduced himself as the head of the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he actually a trained prison warden?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mr. Zoran Sekulovic mentioned himself that he was not a trained prison warden. He came to be the prison warden since August 15, 1993. Prior to that, he studied politics. He had nothing to do with prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he explain to you why he nevertheless became the warden?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, he was jobless and he had to do something in order to survive.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What did he tell you about Mr. Krnojelac? Did he mention him at all?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When he was questioned about the supervision of guards, Mr. Sekulovic mentioned that Mr. Krnojelac was the -- he had to coordinate with a certain person, Marko Arsovic. Mr. Krnojelac himself wasn't a prison -- Mr. Krnojelac was a teacher prior to the war, just like himself, who was now a prison director.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sekulovic tell you why Mr. Krnojelac became a prison warden although he was not a professional in this field?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said everybody had to do something during the war, so he thought that that was the reason why Mr. Krnojelac became what he did at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sekulovic tell you something about the camp as such, or the prison? Let's call it "the prison."

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He stated that the camp consisted of two parts: One part is the military and the other part was the regular prison. The military part was dealt with by the Herzegovina corps. The head of it was General Grubac. And both parts were taken care of by the Minister of Justice, because guards were employed for both sides, the regular and the military.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ask Mr. Krnojelac how they -- how this division between --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you mean Mr. Sekulovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And are we going to find out who the person was that Mr. Krnojelac had to consult? We have a name, but we don't know anything more about him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have before mentioned the name of this Marko - I don't get it now - of this person Mr. Krnojelac had to consult with. Can you repeat the name and tell us who that person was, or what information you got about this person?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sekulovic mentioned that Mr. Krnojelac had to coordinate with a certain Marko Arsovic, but I don't know what Mr. Marko Arsovic's function was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you try to get more information about this coordination and how it worked with the guards being guards for both parts of the prison? Did you try to get more information?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Sekulovic said that the prison complex itself had 50 guards and they had to work 10 shifts. The shift consisted of eight hours. And the first shift was from 6.00 in the morning to 2.00 p.m.; the second shift was from 2.00 p.m. to 10.00 p.m.; and the third shift was from 10.00 p.m. to 6.00 a.m. the following morning. And there was also administrative staff which worked from 7.00 a.m. to 3.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ask Mr. Sekulovic how this staff was divided among the military part and the civilian part and how that would work?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sekulovic said that the guards worked for both parts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you try to find out how they could make this distinction and how Mr. Sekulovic coordinated with the military commander and how Mr. Krnojelac did that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't give us an answer. He just didn't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ask Mr. Sekulovic to provide documentation on the inmates during the relevant times and about the staff?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. I requested for a plan of the prison complex, a list of prison officials, a list of prisoners, but unfortunately he said he couldn't give us that. We had to get it from the Minister of Justice.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you know if you ever got information on the inmates --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- or the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: After this meeting, how did you proceed in the prison?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I proceeded with two policemen and two prison guards. We took photographs, as indicated in the photo album.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you mentioned the two prison guards. Do you recall or have you written down who that was?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guard commander was Mitar Rasevic and his deputy was Miro Prodanovic, accompanied us.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you document all rooms in the prison?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really, because the prison was a really large complex. It would take us two weeks or so to document every single room. And besides, we were only interested in the rooms that were mentioned by witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I forgot to ask you something about what Mr. Sekulovic said. Did he tell you when Mr. Krnojelac left the prison and to which job he then came?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did say that he left the prison, went back -- he was director of the school prior to the war, and after the war -- after he finished at the KP Dom, he went back to teaching in the primary school, if my memory serves me correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we go into the rooms, the actual rooms that you documented, I would like to look -- I would like you to look at the photo 7442. During the testimony of other witnesses, the question was -- the question arose: From which standpoint of view was this photo taken? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was taken from a higher position. I remember we were standing on a steep bank. This was across the road from KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you recall how much higher you were when this photo was made?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately not. I didn't take any measurements of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And with the help of the usher, I would like to show you the photo 7529. Would that be the street level; the same photo, actually, but the street now, from the street level?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Maybe we can also solve another problem at the same time. Would you please show this photo to the witness as well. It's the photo -- I can't see the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, would you please tell us the year and number of this photo, the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arrow is indicating to a bridge. From the position where we took this photograph, we wanted to show whether the bridge was visible from the room that we were viewing it from.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in your -- do you recall which room it was that you made this photo from?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, it was Room 23, right wing, on the third floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Is that the top floor?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the top -- yeah, it is, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It may be rather important. "I think" is not much of an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We return to this photo in a later stage because from this room Ms. Manas made several photos. It's just that it was on the ELMO now, therefore I wanted to address it. But we come to this a little bit later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, let's move to the administration building first, and I would like to -- you to have a look at the photo 7444 and 7445.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, it's on the same sheet.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you also explain to us what we see?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the entrance door to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And on the bottom?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7345, when you enter to the KP Dom to the one I just pointed out to you on your right-hand side, you'll find this is the corridor leading down the right-hand side of the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And did you make photos of the inside of these rooms that we just see here?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They weren't in question at that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And now - with the help of the usher - the photo 7446, what do we see on the photo 7446?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7446, this is on the left-hand side of the administration building when you enter. The arrow down there points to the reception room window. The arrow down there points to the entrance door leading to the administration building, off the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: For the record, the witness was first pointing at the arrow on the left-hand side of the photo, and then to the arrow pointing to the door on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And there's also a board, a show board in this entrance hall, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: A board, a blackboard?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is there, a notice board.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And now I would like you to have a look at the photo 7448, and tell us what we see. There are several numbers, yellow numbers, and can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view showing the ground floor. Number 1 was the corridor leading to the admin. building on your left. This is a reception room that we just passed. And number 2 indicates the door leading, leading to the admin. building, which will take you to the first floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When you are pointing to one of these that does have a number, would you please state the number so that we've got it in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 indicates the passage way on the left-hand side. Number 2 indicates the door that will take you to the administrative building to the first floor. Number 3 indicates a reception door.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Ms. Manas. The next two photos I would like to put in front of you are the photos 7450 and 7451, and it's actually a third one, 7452. In this order, please. What do we see and ...

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7450, 1 indicates the stairway leading up to the first floor, and 2 indicates a cellar underneath the stairway.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, and please say the next photo.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7451, this is a stairway leading up to the first floor, and the arrow indicates the left wing of the prison quarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And would you be able to tell us, when you look through the window on this photo, on which room in the prisoners' quarters would you look?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That will be Room 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And now the next photo, please, 7452. Is this made from the same spot or from a higher level?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I able to consult my notes?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This 7452 is actually the close-up of the window.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the same level.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we have the photo before we -- the photo that we had before, can we have this again on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So would you please double-check. You have there the arrow, the arrow pointing, and as you said, Room 11, and would you now please look again on the photo 7452.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's on a different level.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Is it -- which level is it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That will be on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And the windows -- when you look through the window, onto which room in the prisoners' quarters do you look?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Room 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Now proceeding in the administration building, I would like to have -- I would like you to have a look at the photo 7454. What do we see?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a corridor which is on the right-hand side of the admin. building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Are you sure that it is the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the right-hand side. As you enter up from the stairway, you turn right. This is the right corridor. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could it be the corridor on the left side?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No. Look, please --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's a little bit difficult now. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: She has said quite definitely it was on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, but now I have to use a -- I have to use the floor, the floor plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Exhibit 6/1. We have to find out what "right" and "left" is now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, when you look at this floor plan --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This is actually the ground floor. We have to use the photo 6/2, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's not a photo, it's a plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, could you please point out to us which corridor you meant.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's this corridor --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because as you come up the stairway, I took it -- I'm facing it. It will be my right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas pointed at the right-hand side where there is "Pravna Zgrada" written on. Yes, thank you. I would like to show now to the witness the photos 7457 and 7458.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What do we see on these photos?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7457 shows the inside of Room 17. The arrow indicates this corridor that I pointed out earlier, the one before this, the corridor on your right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And but you say Room 17. Does that mean the rooms were numbered, all these rooms on the floors in the administration were numbered?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all the rooms. Certain rooms had numbers, but the numbers didn't run sequentially. Some of them were mixed up, so this room had number 17 on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we have a look on the lower photo. Would that be -- yes, what is it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is inside Room 17, showing you the opposite side, can be seen through this window which is the left wing of the administrate -- the left wing of prison quarters, Room 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And can we please have again this floor plan, 6/2. Can we -- yes. Would you be able to point out this Room 17?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this floor plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Take your time, take your time and look. Opposite the administration building is the prisoners' buildings, and you see the two wings. Maybe this helps you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, are you asking the witness to point out Room 17 on this floor plan?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's marked on this plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, number 17 in the administration building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, I see, right.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I remember. This is Room 11. It was next to the WC, so it should be that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing on the left part of the administration building, next to the WC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, was she? I thought she was pointing at the second room from the end. You'd better get it clear because --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- the pointer was moving, but I thought that the witness rested it on the second room from the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, go back to the administration building and point out Room 17.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my memory serves me correct, it is next to the WC, and opposite Room 11, so this is Room 11 as shown on this plan, so this should be it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at the room next to the WC room in this sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, that's third from the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, a minute ago , you said that when you pointed out the corridor to us, that it was a corridor in the right wing. How does that then fit?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. You were showing me the first floor of the administration building, and the photo itself was on the right side, right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, now I see. Witness, you only looked -- when you saw the sketch, you looked only on part of it. Is that --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry about the sketch, because I'm not very familiar with the sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I am completely lost, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. It may or may not be important; I don't know. Her document that we received Thursday of last week recounted the order in which she took photographs. I don't know whether that will assist you in determining which photograph we are meant to be looking at.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We are looking at the photograph -- what number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. The one that the witness has said was on the right-hand side of the building and which you're trying desperately to get her to say it's on the left-hand side of the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Because according to the notes as I understood them, it's on the left-hand side, the corridor on the left-hand side, which is now actually confirmed by Ms. Manas, who said that the room number 17 was on this corridor and she could see - as it is now, the photo 7458 - from this room she could look onto room 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, if you're satisfied with it, I won't proceed with the matter any further, but it's very confusing, to say the least.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would now like to show two other photos, and it's the photos -- it's 7459 and 7460. Ms. Manas, is this also on the same floor we just spoke about?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 7459 and 7460 is room 17. The photo just shows the opposite side of the walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And on this floor, when you documented this floor, was there something that -- of interest in there?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7460 you'll find the BiH insignia, the emblem, and also the walls were scraped.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas was pointing at a door on the left-hand side, pointing out a Bosnia-Herzegovina crest.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you said the rooms were scratched. What do you mean by "scratched"?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see -- I don't -- the paint was scraped. Certain parts of the walls were scraped; not the entire room itself, but certain parts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you ask those guards, Mr. Rasevic or the other one who accompanied you, why it was scratched?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Rasevic mentioned that due to the NATO airstrikes, the plaster of the walls had fallen off, so they scraped the walls in order to make it look presentable.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What did you think when he said that? Did you believe that or did you have your own ideas?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not all the rooms were scraped. It's only the rooms that the alleged torture took place were scraped.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In which condition was the entire KP Dom in regard of the walls and the floors and what the rooms looked like?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that -- well, given the circumstances, it didn't look all that bad. Well, just as I mentioned, only certain rooms had particular -- it was particular attention paid to, you'll find the scraping of the walls were done. For the rest of the KP Dom, it was just left in its original state: holes, no plaster was put on those holes or no scrapings were done to neaten (sic) the place up.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And I would like to show you the photo 7461. You pointed -- in the photo before you pointed at a door. Is that the door?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the door with the inscription on it. This is in room 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did the prison staff tell you something about this crest or this drawing?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Rasevic mentioned again that when the Muslims had control of the prison, they had the insignias placed all over. He showed us this door, and down the corridor there was another cupboard with a BiH emblem on it or "BiH" just written on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the photo 7464.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is this the cupboard you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what did you think? Did you believe that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The rest of the rooms were renovated, and just to have these signs left there would be rather strange, especially if they are your enemy. That's the impression I got. Because the rest of the rooms were renovated. Why didn't they clean that out? I don't know. That's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, you said that you also worked there in the evening. What did you do when you were there in the evening?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the evening, Mr. Schouten, he conducted an illumination test to test for the presence of blood, and he took a control sample from the close proximity of the illuminated area, which showed positive; under normal circumstances, it showed positive. And photographs were taken, but unfortunately, it didn't come out clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: First of all, could you explain to the Court what exactly you meant with the illumination test? What is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just before you do that, do we know who Mr. Schouten is?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. We have mentioned him on Friday, that he is a forensic expert from the Dutch laboratories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And has he made a report about any of this?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's included in Ms. Manas' report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'm wondering just what is the value of all of this hearsay material. If it's in a report, it's in a report. What's the point of getting it on a very imprecise hearsay basis from this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have -- it's only -- the report, actually, the report of Ms. Manas and Mr. Schouten is very basic, and it simply says that an illumination test was conducted. And I thought it would be helpful if she would explain what it is, because she was present. It's not that Mr. Schouten was there and Ms. Manas was not there; she was with him all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you want to fill in gaps in a report, by all means go ahead. But if I could go back to an earlier piece of evidence you extracted from this witness as to whether she believed whether somebody else was telling the truth, may I suggest that a more appropriate way to lead that evidence would be: What did you see yourself?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That would enable us to make up our minds as to whether this gentleman was telling the truth. Whether this witness believes he was telling the truth is not terribly helpful.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And she went on to explain it by giving us a description of what she had seen, which demonstrated a reasonable assumption that what the man was saying may not have been correct. But it doesn't help us to have hearsay opinion, which is even worse than hearsay evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So can you tell us briefly what it was that you did, you and Mr. Schouten.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Illumination fluid, which Mr. Schouten sprayed on the suspected area -- he didn't take the control sample from the actual illumination area itself; he took it from the close proximity of the area and he tested it with a tetra-based fluid. And when it turned greenish, it would indicate it's positive. So he took a photograph of the area and control samples.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Where did you make these tests? In which part of the building?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the administration building, first floor, near room 13, near the corridor door of the administration building, and as well as the PTT office on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, the word "positive" worries me.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I have had some experience of blood testing in a number of cases, and the forensic experts have a habit of saying that something proves positive, but you don't know what it means. I found out once in a case - it may have changed since - but "positive" simply meant that it was possible that it was blood of something, an animal or anything, but no more.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And you really need to go a bit further before you can say or suggest that it was human blood. Now, I don't know whether this witness knows what this expert meant by the expression "positive."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We were just going into this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, what did this -- when you say it showed to be positive, what did it actually indicate? What did --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As Your Honour was saying, it could indicate many things, blood or -- as Luminal at that time wasn't a good thing to use for blood because it wasn't specific for blood, because Luminal used during this period in question could also relate to vegetable dyes and detergents, copper-based metal. So one couldn't say that because it was positive green, that blood was present.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Therefore what did you do to clarify the matter? Did you request a forensic lab to examine?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The swabs that Mr. Schouten had taken, the control and the test, were sent to the Dutch forensic lab.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you receive a result?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. The results showed negative.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. We would like to enter into evidence the result of the lab, and it's actually ID in our photo binder 42.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P42.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could the illumination fluid have altered -- had an effect on the results from the forensic lab?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, that Mr. Schouten said that, at the time in question, we used illumination fluid which is rather different from what we use today, and that could have had an effect on the test, because for various reasons - the surface could have been washed with a detergent, the paint could have had vegetable dyes or might have had a copper base - so that could change the results of the test.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. You just mentioned the PTT room. Where was it in the building?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What can you tell us about this room? Did you go into this PTT room?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Well, I was curious to see -- there was a brownish stain leading from the entrance of the door to the inside of the room. The carpet, the stain was in the carpet.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you make photos of the PTT room?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But I couldn't see any in the binder. Why not?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time, it wasn't in question, so I didn't place those photos in the binder itself, but I have it with me if the Court would like to see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like you to put an example of this onto the ELMO. Ms. Manas, the photos that you did from the PTT room, are they all like this, or do you have photos that show the entire room, or that really --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We, we only have the picture of the carpet, that's it, because Mr. Schouten conducted a test with a tetra-based fluid, and the control sample at that stage was negative; but in order to be 100 per cent sure, we took further samples to have them tested at the lab.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So we don't have any photos that show us the entire PTT room at all?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do not want to enter this into evidence. It was just to show that we do not have better photos that could really help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Should it be given an identification number?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We actually didn't intend to hand it to the, to the record. It's just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But nevertheless --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- it would be preferable. It doesn't mean it goes into evidence, it's just we do know which document the witness was looking at.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What number are we up to, the mark for identification documents?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it will be identification number 414.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Identification number C-1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's not C at all. What is the last document that was marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be 3, mark for identification 3. That document will be marked for identification "3." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm told that we already have a 3, so it will be marked for identification "4."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, before we go to the prisoners' quarters, I would like you to have a look at the photos 7462 and 7463. What does it show? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the entrance of the WC.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On which floor, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first floor of the admin. building, which is next to the Room 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And below, the photo below?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photo below is taken from the second door off the WC, showing the opposite view of the left wing room, number 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the yellow arrows, do they indicate this Room 11?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show now the witness the photos 7469, 7470, and 7471.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Ms. Manas, would you please explain to us what we see on these photos?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On 7469, 1 shows you the entrance door to the waiting room, 2 is the entrance door to the prison quarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And the next photo? The arrow, what does it point at?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7470, this is the waiting room. The arrow points to the metallic door that will take you to the prison quarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you call it a waiting room. Why do you call it a waiting room?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the prisoners -- after handing over their property, visitors wait here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the last of these photos, what is it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is taken from the inside of the prison complex. This is the metallic door that we referred to in the previous photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Before you move to the next one, I want to get this document marked for identification business sorted out. I thought I had before. The document that you showed the witness, where is it now?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Which document do you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The one that you said you did not want to tender, and I said I wanted it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That was simply the photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But where is the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It is with Ms. Manas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, then, could you please retrieve it, Usher, so that the court deputy can actually mark it with a number and sign it so that later on it can be identified as the document shown to the witness, if we need to have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting, but if you allow us, the Defence would like to see the photograph. We only saw it when it was on the ELMO, but we would like to see it later on as well and perhaps use it, if we need to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sure that the Prosecution will show it to you. They don't want to tender it at this stage, but you should get that directly from them. We do not have custody of it. All we have, the court deputy will mark it with a number and some form of identification that it has been shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: If it is, if it is more helpful for the Court and for the Defence, we can tender it. I mean, it's only -- it's not actually -- it has no probative value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's why we didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'll leave it to you to sort out with Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can tender it into evidence, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you have any objection to it becoming an exhibit, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The next number is what, 410?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Fourteen. It will be P414.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put again the photo 7528 to the witness. It's the top, photo on the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have already mentioned -- you have already mentioned this photo, and you said that it is the view from Room 23, but when we look into your photo binder, it actually says, "View from Room 28." Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That must have been a typing error because my notes correctly refer to as 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And with the help of the usher, to clarify the matter, can we have the Exhibit 6/5 put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, this is a sketch of the -- showing the prisoners', especially the prisoners' quarters, and it's the -- this is the third floor. Can you -- and you see on the sketch it's indicated Room 23. Is that -- would that be correct --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- according to your memory --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- and your notes?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be correct. Actually, there's two rooms 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And the photo was taken from which of the two rooms 23, the left or the right one; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check my notes for that. The room on the right, be this room. And I was facing the room, so it would be on my right. There.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing on the second room counted from the left -- from the right, sorry. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Does that mean -- we can't quite see it from the edge, and I don't have my own copy here. It is not the corner room but the one next to the corner room?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is that correct, Ms. Manas?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: From this room, you can see, you can see on the photo, you can see the river, the River Drina, and part of the bridge, as you said before. Do you recall if you could see the bridge over the Drina from a lower floor?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the photo 7472 and 7473.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you tell us from where -- from which point have you made this photo?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7472, it was taken from Room 23 in the right wing. 1 indicates the metallic door, 2 is the roof of the admin. building on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And we have here the photo, another photo. Can you tell us what it shows?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7473, this photo was taken from the right wing of the prison quarters where both the left -- the left of the admin. building, facing the left wing of the prison quarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This is indicated -- the left wing is indicated with number 2 on the photo?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you measure the distance between this point of view, that is, the block -- the right block, and the administration building, did you measure it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And what did you find?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe if we put the photo after this which shows the full windows, it's easier to -- for the Court to understand what I'm trying to say. It would be 7476, I think. The first window on my right facing the admin. building measured up to 11.75 metres; the second window measured up to 11.15 metres; the third, 10.70 metres; and the fourth, 10.20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you were pointing now at which room?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Room 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So these were the distances to the administration building?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Administration building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. But I actually asked you about the distance between the other block, the other block and the administration building.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right wing?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, the right wing. That is, can you tell us how far that was?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it okay if I put my notes on the ELMO, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you think that that will help us?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If it does, please do so.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the right wing. From the left corner of right wing to the entrance to admin. building, it's 30.80 metres, an extreme right of the right wing is 41 metres to the entrance of the admin. building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: May I suggest, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, that we have that sketch reproduced on another piece of paper and then we can have it as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, we can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We don't want to put the witness's book into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No. Yes, we will produce it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let me just refer to your report, to the report that we have already entered into evidence. Did you make a drawing of Room 11 and measure the drawing?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we have it on the ELMO? Your Honour, it is part of Prosecution Exhibit 41.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, can you put it on the ELMO and explain just the measures. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's spavaona 1 and spavaona 2 are actually the rooms that face the administration building, and 3 and 4 faces the rear of the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, you all have it at hand; therefore, we do not need to go into the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I only wonder why you called it "spavaona"?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the name that was written on the door itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And does it mean "bedroom" in the --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. That should be enough. When you went to this Room 11, was Mr. Rasevic still with you?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was there all the time with us. He accompanied us everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did he tell you something about the use of this room during the relevant time?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that the Room 11 wasn't used since April 11th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ask him such a question or did he volunteer it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We just volunteered it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Did you visit the isolation cells when you went to make your photos?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the photo 7524 and 7519.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what we see on the first photo and the second one.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the isolation cell on the left-hand side. 1, 2, 3, 4 are the four isolation cells on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the other photo?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7519 is the isolation cell on the right-hand side. 1, 2, and 3 indicates the isolation cell itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And also now the photo 7525 and 7526.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness switch on the other microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Is that one of such isolation cells?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 7525 is inside of one of the isolation cells.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And the other one?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7526 is a toilet in the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you conduct forensic experiments in this section while you were there?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you find any clear message from the walls in relation to what might have happened in the rooms?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was lots of bloodstain, but it would be inconclusive because Mr. Rasevic mentioned that prisoners, especially drug addicts, were detained in these rooms, and when they ended up fighting with each other -- so it's possible that you would find blood there. And it's not -- he also mentioned that if blood was found, it's not to be taken that prisoners were mistreated. And before the war, prisoners used to inflict injuries on themselves in order to be moved out of the hospital. And during the war, they had no prison facilities for injured prisoners, so the injured prisoners were kept in these isolation blocks, so you would find blood because of injuries, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And while you were in these isolation cells, did you find any writings on the walls?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we found some writings on the wall. They looked like -- some of the names that appeared on the wall were Muslim names, indicating a detention period from 1992 to 1995. Some of the messages were very sad. They appeared to be the final words to one's loved one. Unfortunately, I cannot recall every single -- I don't recall any of the words written there. And we also didn't make a photograph of this so-called writing on the wall because it was very faint and Mr. Schouten thought it wouldn't be -- it wouldn't come out clear if it was photographed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And how did this make you feel, these messages on the walls? Did it have an effect on you?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was very emotionally devastating. It, as I said, was like a condemned prisoner's final words of farewell to one's loved one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have already entered into evidence the Exhibit P42, the reports from the forensic lab. Did they also examine explosives? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. Those metal fragments were taken out from the wall of the restaurant which is opposite the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the photos 7530 and 7531.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you show us first on the top photo what these numbers 1 and 2 indicate.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On 7530, number 1 indicates the restaurant opposite the KP Dom; number 2 is the KP Dom complex itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And the photo below?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7531, actually, the restaurant's front entrance facing the KP Dom, bullet holes or indention marks, as you can see on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why did you make photos of this particular building and why did you take metal fragments to the lab?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some witnesses that were detained in the KP Dom alleged that they heard shooting outside the prison complex, which is near the restaurant, and seeing this, we thought this -- well, we thought this is what the witness was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why did you think that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looked like a shooting scene to me, because there were indention marks from left to right and right to left and at a certain height.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And were these -- what were these fragments that you pulled out of the wall? Was it examined and with which result? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was examined and the metal fragments were connected to explosives.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the details you find in the written report on this matter. Yes. These are the questions that the Prosecution has of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Cross-examination. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I will start from the end, from the last question that my colleague posed. I would like the witness to explain to me or to clarify to me that these indentions on the restaurant originated from explosives. Could we be more precise and hear whether there was a shrapnel trace or a -- what caused these marks?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a ballistic expert to answer that question. According to the forensic report, it shows -- the metal fragments were remains of an exploded grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is what my question related to. And now I will go back to the beginning of your today's testimony, when you were showing a photograph of the bridge in Brod and damage on that bridge. You linked it to the massacre of Muslims. And I want to know whether you, with the help of a forensic expert, a ballistic expert, were able to establish what was the calibre. Were those bullet damages or they perhaps were damages from shrapnel or grenades? Because as you probably know, the fighting in Foca lasted for about ten days.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, we didn't have a ballistic expert with us, and I for one cannot say that it was the scene of a massacre. As I explained to you, that witnesses alleged that shooting took place on the bridge, and seeing these traces of bullet holes or indention, I had the photographs taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What I want to know is: Are you sure that those were the marks left by bullets?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Have you noticed that on the side -- there were some damages on the side and on the rear side? Were you able to observe that, that there are damages on various parts?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were damages on various parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: These marks that you saw at the restaurant and at the bridge, are those the only ones that you encountered in the town of Foca?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the buildings that I was viewing, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also talked about room number 18 in the administrative building -- room number 17, I apologise, in the administrative building. I would like you to explain or tell us how many floors the administrative building has.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, offhand I cannot tell you unless I look at my photographs. We only went to the first floor of the administration building, and we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. viewed the rooms that were in question at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: May I just clear up that, Mr. Bakrac? By "the first floor," do you mean the American ground floor or the European next floor up?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's ground floor and then first floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Thank you. That was my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know what is located above that room on the first floor and how many flights further up there are?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't go to that -- the other parts of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what was the reason for your going straight to this room number 17 and not anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the room that overlooks room number 11 of the left wing of the prison quarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is that the only room in the administration building from which you have the view of the room number 11 of the prison part?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This room on your extreme left, the -- as you see through the photographs, the cupboard with the BiH sign, the blue cupboard, next to that there was a room that was also numbered room number 11. You could see part of room 11 of lettering of admin. building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly when you were answering the Prosecution's questions, when you pointed to the exit from the room 17, you stated that that was the exit into the hallway that you identified and showed first in the photograph and then on a drawing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were discussing the information that you received from the current warden of the KP Dom, is it true that he stated to you that he became a warden exactly on the 15th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it also true that he stated that Milorad Krnojelac was not a warden as of August 1993 and that he went to his old profession after that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you were talking about Mr. Sekulovic telling you that KP Dom was divided into two parts - one was civilian and the other one was under the command of the Herzegovina corps - and that there were guards there, did he also tell you at the time that there were guards who were under the military command and also guards who were under the command of civilian authorities, or did he tell you that all guards were under the civilian authority's command or all guards were under the command of the military authorities?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No; it was clear that it was two separate guards, one for the military and for the regular prison, but they both fell under the Minister of Justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In what sense do you mean they all fell under the Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I understood from Mr. Sekulovic, that Minister of Justice was responsible for these guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you aware -- did you encounter in your research work, did you encounter the fact that these guards, at certain intervals when they were working and staying in KP Dom, also went to the front line?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If you allow such a possibility, do you think that the Ministry of Justice was able to send them to the front line, or was it perhaps Ministry of Defence or military authorities? What is your opinion? Since we already heard some of your conclusions, what is your opinion on this?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have an opinion on that. That is what Mr. Sekulovic said, that these two parts fell under the Minister of Justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you to go back to the beginning of your testimony when you stated that upon arriving in Foca and conducting your research work in the neighbourhoods of Aladza, Donje Polje, Gornje Polje, and the old centre of town, that you saw some burned buildings there which you believed were Muslim houses. My question is the following: Were you able to establish the number of houses destroyed and who were the owners of those houses?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we didn't have that opportunity of doing such, because we were escorted by the police, and at the time it wasn't safe to go around and do your normal interviews and asking people which house belonged to who.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, but you would agree that we have some statements from the ground, dating back to 1999, and we also have a beginning set of photographs that you showed, showing the work that was carried out in September of 2000. Were you not able to establish this fact so that we have no doubts as to whose houses were in fact destroyed?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure it must have been done with the investigative team. I worked with the team for a short period and I worked in many other investigations after that, so I cannot give you a definite answer in regards to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll resume at 11.30, then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, before the break, we established that the owner -- that you had not identified the owners of damaged houses. Now I should like to ask you to look at a photograph - and I need the help of the usher - and tell me if you can tell us what you see on that. It is 40, 7209 [as translated]. So tell us what you see on this photograph and what it is about.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7290, you see a few damaged houses and a mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said a few damaged houses and a mosque. Is there a number of houses around the mosque which are intact?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see by the picture.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When my learned friend asked you, you said that you thought those were Muslim houses because they were located around the mosque. Are you claiming that all these other houses belong to Serbs, and does that mean that the inference that only Muslim houses around the mosque is correct?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't say that there are only Muslim houses around the mosque. I don't know why the houses around the mosque was only damaged; I cannot answer that. And I'm also not saying that the houses surrounding that which are not damaged doesn't belong to Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But in your testimony you said, according to the transcript, that you thought it was a Muslim locality because there was a mosque there, and that from that you inferred that the destroyed houses belonged to Muslims.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So all the other houses which had not been destroyed were Serb houses, or are Serb houses, are they?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't show whether it is Muslim or Serb. That's why I say I cannot rule out the possibility it might have been Muslim houses because it is a Muslim neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you exclude the possibility that there are also some Serb-owned houses amongst those destroyed?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So are there only Muslim houses next to the mosque, or are you allowing the possibility for some Serb houses in that same neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know if there were Serb houses in this neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. There was also evidence about samples which were taken here to test them for blood, and naturally the analysis said that the tests were negative, that is, that the presence of blood was not established. What worries me, however, is that in your report, or rather, in your observations during the investigation, you nevertheless stated that there were some indications about the presence of blood; and in today on transcript, on page 21, line 20, you said that green pigmenting was a proof of the presence of blood. However, you also told us that when you talked to the person who did those analyses with you, you learnt that green staining can also appear because -- in the presence of some other chemicals, detergents or some other stuff.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The test conducted can also give a false positive for various reasons, as I explained. It could be detergents, vegetables dyes, or copper-based metals, which Luminal is not specific for blood. When the tetra-based test was done for blood on the control sample, it indicated positive. It turned greenish.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The chemical which turned greenish, could it also turn green in the presence of another chemical, that is, a dye, a paint, detergent, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the reading can give you a false positive, and I cannot get into details about this because it's not my area of training.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I agree. But in the transcript on page 21, line 20, you said that it proved the presence of blood; and in your report on page 5, paragraph 4, you also said there was proof of the presence of blood. Now you tell us that it could have been some other chemical. Can we then agree that you found no proof, no evidence of the presence of blood on the samples that you tested?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the control test indicated positive --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, no. Look --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the reason why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, the evidence which this witness has given is no doubt what she genuinely believes, but she is not an expert. She has conceded it is wrong. How can we possibly rely upon anything that she has said about blood?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
