utterances.text: Salko Mandzo told us that he was beaten and that one of the Chetniks said, "Don't beat him anymore because I will slash his throat." And then he realised that this was not Emir whom he in fact wanted, and then he was brought back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Kuo, is there a pseudonym that is involved here?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. In fact, they're two different people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I know that, but was one of them afforded a pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Good, thank you. I was only concerned about redacting the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. Just as a note of explanation, there's a Fuad Mandzo who has been mentioned, and then Emir Mandzo, and this witness has identified Emir Mandzo as being a medical technician. And in fact, Emir Mandzo is listed in Schedule B at number 37.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you give us the names of people you knew who were taken out during this time and that you never saw again?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Two men with the last name Veiz, and if you allow me, could I look into my notes again?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And this, for the record, is what's been identified as ID number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now marked for identification 5. It is a subtle difference. The documents in your folders are ID with numbers; these are MFI, marked for identification 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the Defence be given this paper that the witness is using so that we could compare it to the materials that we have?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I was told that you have been given a copy of it when we started discussing it earlier on this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. We were given copies, but we simply wanted to make sure that the copy is the same as the original in the witness's possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, you want to check your copy with what he's got. I suppose that's fair enough because we didn't have the actual document out. Yes, Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Sir, you were able to look at your document now.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I could tell this, but in order to save time and in order to save me effort, because I have been through a lot, I suffered a lot, and sometimes I cannot recollect everything instantly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: That's fine. You can tell us, then, the names of the two Veizes.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Two men with the name -- last name Veiz, Veiz, Zulfo was a policeman with Foca SUP; and the other one was a worker, Selimovic Haso; Nisic, Nurko; Kiselica, Esad; Dzano, Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Please slow down because I need to tell the Judges something after each name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: For the record, Zulfo Veiz is on Schedule C, number 29.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Sir, you didn't give us the first name of the other Mr. Veiz.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Munib.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Munib Veiz is Schedule C, number 28. Nurko Nisic is Schedule C, number 19, and --

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Selimovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Esad Kiselica is Schedule C, number 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What he was doing was correcting you, you see. He said Selimovic, and you have recorded it as Nurko Nisic. At least, that's what you are recorded as having said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that, Your Honour, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I did not get the name of Selimovic. He's not on Schedule C, but he's on a different schedule, so we're going to look that up right now. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The last one was Esad Dzano.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Esad Dzano is also not on Schedule C but on a different schedule.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Okay. If you could just proceed, then. Who else was taken out that day, or those days?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Konjo, Halid.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: On Schedule C, Your Honours, number 13 is listed as Halim Konjo, and we think that that's the same name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Prosecution -- Prosecutor said that she believed that that's the same person, but this is for the witness to say, so whether it's the same person or two different individuals. Prosecutor just stated before the witness that she believed that was the same person, but it was up for the witness to say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You're quite right. There has been both names used during the course of the trial in relation to Konjo, Halim and Halid, so you'd better find out precisely which one the witness means and accept it when he says it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was there also a Halim Konjo?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Halid, with a "D."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So they're two different people, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: This is just one person. His name is Konjo, Halid. He had a brother, but his brother is not on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was his brother Halim?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've now found the names, the references to Hasan Dzano. It's on Schedule B, number 18, and Hasan Selimovic is on Schedule B, number 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Sir, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Emir Mandzo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: That's already been identified to the Court.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Ramovic, Hamid.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: He has likewise being identified as Schedule C, number 20.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Tulek, Kemal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Is that -- is his name also Tulek, Kemal?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: He is Schedule C, number 25.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Balic, Serif, and his son. I don't know the son's first name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Those two have already been identified to the Court.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Dzelilovic, Kemal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: He is on Schedule C, number 7.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: And some others that I was not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'm looking at a copy of your same notes, and you have two other names listed. Hodzic, Nail?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, yes. And also Dzendusic, Ramo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Hodzic, Nail is on Schedule C, number 10, and Dzendusic, Ramo, is Schedule C, number 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were there other people whose names you wrote down a little bit later who were also taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: There were. They also took away two brothers with the last name Rikalo, and their relative.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know their first names?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, there were three Rikalos listed on Schedule C, numbers 22, 23, and 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And was there anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not know if this is an error or what. The witness said two men called Rikalo. No, two Rikalos and a relative.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: It's three.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were there three people with the last name Rikalo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He's already said that, and their relative, he said.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Correct, correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He said that before the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, who was the last person that you listed?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Kruno. He's Croat who was a TV repairman in Foca, and a nurse, a Croat, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You said Kruno. Was that his nickname or a real name?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Last name, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, on Schedule C, number 17, there is a Marinovic, Krunoslav who has been identified by other people as being a Croat, and we believe that that is the same person.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Just to clarify, when you said Kruno and he was a TV repairman, and then you said something about being a nurse, was that the same person or was that a different person?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They are two different persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was the name of the other person, the one who was not Kruno?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but he worked at the otorhinological ward because I often went there to have my ears checked, so I knew him from there. But I knew him by sight, I didn't know -- I not know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was that person also a Croat?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. And he was in Room 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, other witnesses have identified Schedule C, number 11, Mate Ivancic, as being a Croat nurse, and we believe that that is the right person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know. I apologise, but where is this examination going to take us? The witness said he did not know the name, not that he could not remember. And now when the Prosecutor said that she believed it was that person, then the witness said, "Yes, that is the person."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's a matter that goes to the weight of the answer. I don't think there's anything really that you can do about it now. The witness offered it, he wasn't asked the question, and we will place such weight upon it as appears to us to be necessary later, but I'm not going to exclude it. Yes, Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that after Hamid Ramovic was taken to the gate, you heard a car. Did you hear a car after anyone else was taken away?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I did. Nail Hodzic and Ramo Dzendusic were taken away in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know where the car went?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Towards the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: After these incidents that you described a few days around Vidovdan, did other people disappear from the KP Dom, other detainees?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, on St. Vitus's Day or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: We've also discussed what happened on St. Vitus's Day, unless you want to add anything to that.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Right. Quite right. No, I have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The question is: After that day, did other groups of people disappear?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They did not disappear in the same way, because allegedly the exchange had started.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the procedure was for when people were taken out and told they would be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: The policeman on duty would come, or I don't know what you call him, with a list, and he would go to the room, the door of number 13, and would read out the names of people from 13 and he would say, "You get ready, because you are about to be exchanged."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And then what would happen to those people?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: And then they would go to the gate and out, and after that, I don't know, but they would leave the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: On what dates did this happen?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: The exchanges began in late July, because at that time we were quite a number. And one could not really remember who is going, because when there are 600 people, then it's difficult if only 10 men leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were taken out from July?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: All in all or ...?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You said it was hard to keep track of people when they were taken out. Did there come a time when you were able to keep track of people?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Can you estimate about how many people were taken out that you were not able to keep track of? Before you started keeping track, how many people were taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Around 500, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When did you start keeping track of who was taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: On the 31st of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: That morning, between 50 and 55 men left. It was the first large group that left.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened to them?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They were taken away in the morning, but they came back in the evening, and I learnt from them that they had been to Niksic and then turned back to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did all 50 or 55 of them stay in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No. The next morning, they singled out 20 and took them away in an unknown direction, and those 30, 34, 35, they returned to their room and stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Of the 20 people who were taken out at that time, were there elderly people?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was the age of the oldest person that you know in that group?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Ninety.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you remember when -- the date of another exchange?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I do. After the 31st of August, I remember almost all the exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Before we move on, I forgot to ask you about the 31st of August. Were you able to see outside the window when these people were being taken away?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I could, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did anybody threaten you not to look?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the man on duty. He told us to move away from the window.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who was the man on duty who told you that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: What I heard sounded like Obren Obrenovic, but I'm quite sure about the last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Tell us, then, about the next exchange. How many people were taken out and when was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: The next exchange took place on the 10th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How many people were taken out then?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: More than ten.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How were they taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They were taken before lunch, again called out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And when they were called out, who called them out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, whoever was on duty, I mean one of the guards who was on duty, they invariably would read the list out and the list would be brought from the administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened to those ten people?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that any one of them is alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When was the next group taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: The next group left on the 12th of September again, 1992, after lunch, I mean after 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How were they taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They were again called out, except that in this group they were all 25 -- aged 25 to 30, and that included my cousin, my nephew, who was 27, so I remember that particular exchange very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How many people were in that group?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: About 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened to your nephew? Did you ever see him again?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you ever see any of that group of people again?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No, none of them from that group, and I knew quite a number of people in that group.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When was the next group taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: The next group, September -- ah, yes. On the 17th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened then? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: That morning, before breakfast, the guards came and asked for volunteers to pick plums, and that's why I called that group plum pickers. Twenty men left then. But they never volunteered. Again, a list was brought and their names were read out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did the guards ask for volunteers?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You said they never volunteered. Did people come forward when the guards asked for volunteers?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, some, but they insisted on Sulejman Celik; they wanted him to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was Sulejman Celik from your room?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: He was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you ever see him again after that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No. He was found dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: At Previla, which was a hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know when he was found dead?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I think his body was exhumated -- I think the exhumation took place last year, or not long ago, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the other men among the plum pickers?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I know Konjo's brother was also found and buried.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Konjo -- I can't remember the first name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know the brother's name, the one who was found dead?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No. It eludes me, and I don't think I even wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When the guards took out these plum pickers, as you call them, were they told what to bring with them?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were told they were going to pick plums. They would not allow them to take their affairs with them. They told them that they would get uniforms to pick plums instead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So did those people leave their belongings behind?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did they ever come -- did anybody ever come to fetch their belongings for them?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When did the next group get taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Same day, afternoon, 15 men, plums again. They said they were short of labour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened to those 15 men?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They are gone. Not one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When was the next group taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: The next group was taken away on the 18th, but some of them are still alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The 18th of September; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Correct, yes, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were those men told that they would be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They were not told that they would be going to pick plums. They were told that they would be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And after the 18th, when was the next group?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: On the 31st of October, 30 men left.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What were the circumstances under which they left?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: It was men from Nevesinje who came and took them away, and it was said that 30 of them were going for 10 Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you ever see any of those 30 again?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I did. I did. They're alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When was the next group taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: In December 1992. On the 18th -- no. On the 8th of December, 1992, 12 men left.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What were the circumstances under which they left?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Same thing. They were called out -- their names were called out for exchange.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you ever see those people again?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I remember those on the 12th, I remember those better, not the other group.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So on the 8th of December, did you ever see those 12 people again, or are you saying you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I don't. I don't. I don't remember that group, but I know that there were 12 of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And then on the 12th of December was a group taken?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Eight men.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How were those eight taken?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Again, the names were called out and they were to be exchanged, but, but about them I find out when I got to Kula on the 23rd of October, 1993. I found there that friend of mine in the camp at Kula.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did that friend tell you happened to those eight people?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: My friend said, "When we left the administrative building, they immediately took off all the clothes that we had that were any good, and beat us there."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Inside the administrative building or outside?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: In front. In front of the administrative building, right in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did your friend say who beat them? Were they guards or soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened after these men were beaten?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Then they put them onto that small car, "Pivovara" and took them in the direction of Kalinovik.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And you mentioned that your friend was one of these eight people, so obviously you saw him later. What happened to the others?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And after the 12th of December, do you remember any other groups being taken out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No, there were no more groups. In 1993 on the 5th of May, Dr. Ibro Karovic was taken away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: All right. Did a journalist ever come visit you or other detainees in KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: It was in 1992 before the plum pickers left. It was in September, early September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who was the journalist?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They said they came from Duga, an independent paper from Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What room did they visit?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They visited my room, 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did they want to know?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They came and said they had nothing with the authorities, that they were independent, and that we could -- that we could tell them everything, how we had been treated, we were being treated, what they were doing to us, et cetera, et cetera, and that they would not tell them anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did any of the detainees talk to the journalist?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Sulejman Celik discussed things with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did Sulejman Celik tell the journalists?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: He said, "You're too late. It's too late to ask about us because very many of ours, many of us, many Muslims, have already been taken away from the camp."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did he explain anything further to the journalist?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, he complained a little, but he mostly spoke about the disappearance of people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the journalist?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: There was no reaction, only later. When they left, that evening as we were coming back from the dinner, Sulejman was stopped and then beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who stopped him?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Guards, guards in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Where was Sulejman Celik beaten?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: In front of the solitary cell.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And what happened to him further?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Further when they needed volunteers, they looked for him right away. And when people volunteered but they were not happy with those, then they brought a list, and the first name on that list was the name of Sulejman Celik.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you say "volunteer," what was the volunteering for?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Plum picking.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you say anything to the journalist?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I did not because I knew it was fake. I knew they were their men.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Nobody independent could come, could get there. Nobody who was not connected with them could go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did any of the other detainees in your room other than Sulejman Celik speak to the journalist?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, but those were all just, just stories.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What do you mean by that? What did they tell him?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, they wanted to be released. Would they write in their paper that they were in the camp, that their names were such and such. Would they plead with the Red Cross or with the authorities, intercede on our behalf.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: But did those detainees tell the journalists what was happening in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No, they did not dare. Only Sulejman Celik. He just said it inadvertently, and I think that he was sorry later on that he had spoken.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were people -- were detainees ever asked to make blood donations?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: It was in the beginning, in May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know anybody who donated blood?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I do. Veiz -- I mean, Munib, because he was a blood donor even before the war, and I think he donated blood on two occasions, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know if these blood donations were voluntary or not?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: It was voluntary at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know who the warden of KP Dom was when you were there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Milorad Krnojelac, Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you know Milorad Krnojelac from before the war?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you ever see him at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did you see him doing?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I learned that he was the KP Dom warden.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How did you learn it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I learned it from his colleague, Rasim Jusufovic, and Tafro, a manager from the Maglic Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know whether detainees had contact with Milorad Krnojelac at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What kind of contact did they have?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They would say it to the guard that they'd like to see the warden.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And were they permitted to do that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Some of them did go to see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know what they went to see the warden about?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I remember that Cankusic went to inquire -- to ask about the whereabouts of his sons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Where were his sons, do you know?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They were taken away on St. Vitus's Day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So Mr. Cankusic's sons were at KP Dom and then taken away?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was his first name, Mr. Cankusic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I think that I did not write it down.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know the names of Mr. Cankusic's sons?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for reference, and we're not asking this witness to give this testimony, but on Schedule C at numbers 3 and 5, there are -- I'm sorry, at numbers 3 and 4 are two people listed with the last name Cankusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Whilst we've just got this interruption, when this document that he's been referred to first came up, he said that he prepared it when he was first invited to come here and when he was preparing his evidence. Could we have some idea as to when that was? It may have some weight in determining how we approach this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When did you start preparing this document? Do you remember the approximate month, let's say?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, this was not written down when I was scheduled or planned to come here to testify. I wrote this down about six months prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So was this last year that you started to prepare this document?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, because I knew that I would come here to testify.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You said Mr. Cankusic spoke with Krnojelac, inquiring about the whereabouts of his two sons. Did he tell you what Mr. Krnojelac told him had happened?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: That his sons were sentenced and that they went to serve their term.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did he say where?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: In Bileca.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And were specifics given about what they were sentenced for?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't say specifically. He simply said that they were on some kind of a list, and then he inquired and asked, "Why did you beat them so much?" And he replied they had to in order to have them confess. Now, what is it that they confessed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did Mr. Cankusic tell you himself about this conversation?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: He told me, and he was in the Room 12, and there was a window there. And his relatives, his neighbours, asked him whether he knew something about his sons, and he told me what I've just told you, and this is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you ever see or hear yourself detainees complain to Mr. Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear that. I simply know that some people asked to go and see him, to go and talk to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was there a time when you, when you heard Mr. Krnojelac say something about the food that you were receiving?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear once. When -- after -- when we just after the lunch went out and we were standing in line in front of the restaurant because we always had to stand in line, he said, and I don't know whether -- I don't know who in fact asked him, "Mr. Warden, could you improve the food," and he replied, "I distribute everything that I receive."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did he say anything else about why you all were there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Krnojelac on any other occasion?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I did until they opened a restaurant across from the KP Dom. Prior to that, he would go to have lunch there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know how long Milorad Krnojelac was warden of KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I believe until August of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened in August of 1993?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: A new warden came, Zoran Sekulovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did he make any statement to the detainees about how things would be at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you know Savo Todovic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: From what I heard, he was a deputy warden.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How did he treat the detainees?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, he instilled fear in detainees.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How did he do that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, when Zekovic escaped, he put the entire population of the working room into the confinement, solitary confinement, and a number of people survived, and I heard from them how he beat them at the time and how he told them that he would kill them all unless they catch Zekovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were you present when this was happening? I mean, did you see him do this?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I didn't see that. I was in my room and this was taking place in the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you know Mitar Rasevic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I did. He was a commander of the security.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How did he treat detainees?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, he would come into our rooms on a number of occasions and ask us how -- inquire as to how they treated us. He would inquire as to how his staff treated us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did people tell him?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, nobody dared complain. We simply asked him to increase our food rations, because the food that was left after dinner would be thrown away, so we simply asked that it be distributed to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was that done?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: It was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were there guards who did not mistreat prisoners, or did all the guards mistreat the detainees?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: There were some that did not mistreat us, but very few.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When were you taken away from KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I was taken away on the 23rd of October of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I was taken to a camp at Kula in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were you told why you were taken there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No. I was taken there. Zoran Matovic, who was on duty, came in, called out my name, and said, "You are going to Sarajevo as part of an exchange."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the Kula camp?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: About ten months.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you have a choice about whether to stay in the Kula camp or go anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I did not have a choice. I was brought there and delivered there. I had no choice.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you ever see anybody from -- any of the prison staff, the staff from the KP Dom, at the Kula camp? Did anybody come visit?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Todovic with another man, and I think I was going to lunch when he saw me and he asked me, "Hadzimusic, aren't you exchanged yet? If you don't like it here, let's go back with me to Foca." I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. replied that I was almost ready to get into the APC and that I am about to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When were you finally exchanged?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I was exchanged on July 17th, 1994, at the bridge called Bratstvo-Jedinstvo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: In what city?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: As a result of the time that you spent in the KP Dom, could you tell us what physical suffering you underwent.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I have hypertension, cardiac arrhythmia, my blood pressure goes up and down, I have an increased blood sugar, I am tense, and also some problems with my head. I have difficulty remembering names, and this is why I use this list, to trigger my memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you suffer emotionally as a result of being detained at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Can you describe to us what?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. The best years of my life were those years. When I entered KP Dom I was 47 years old and I was full of life, full of enthusiasm, and now I have trouble sleeping. At the time, I had everything I needed and now I don't have anything. I am not looking forward to anything anymore, because I can't laugh or cry anymore. Before, I used to like to sing and now I can't even whistle properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Cross-examination. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Hello. Let me introduce myself. I'm counsel Vasic, Defence counsel for the accused Krnojelac. Could you tell us, please, whether you had given statements to the investigators of the Prosecution with respect to this case.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement on the 2nd of June of 1999?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I have trouble recollecting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And also on the 19th of April, 1996?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I have trouble remembering dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Based on your current testimony -- we heard quite a number of dates today, so I don't know what to think, whether you remember dates well or perhaps those dates that were mentioned by you today are not correct.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: They are correct, all of them, and I remember all dates after August 31st, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Then do you remember the August of 1996 [as interpreted] and 2nd June of 1999?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I remember the dates that I mentioned today because those were my friends and neighbours that were taken away. I had nothing else to do, so I had no trouble remembering those dates. But the dates that you mention, I have trouble remembering them, because my life has changed today. I don't have an apartment, I -- my future is uncertain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I know we have to go through this every time, but please remember, you are speaking the same language, it's the same interpreter that has to take both the question and the answer, and they have to catch up. So would you please pause, Mr. Vasic, before you ask a question, pause at the end of the answer. And Mr. Hadzimusic, would you pause after you hear the question, just for a few moments, before you give the answer, to enable the translator to catch up. That translator there was able to carry nearly five minutes of testimony in their memory, which was a pretty good effort, but you shouldn't really put them to that test.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please, whether investigators from the Prosecution came to ask you about the events pertaining to the KP Dom in Foca.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: What do you mean? Come and see me where?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Since the statement does not indicate where the interview took place, so I suppose that they went to see you at the place where you lived at the time.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, they came and spoke to me in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: How many times did they visit you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember which year they came to visit you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I could not really think about that, because I struggled. I had a daily struggle for life, so I couldn't give you precisely which year it was when they came to visit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you prepare yourself for the interview with the representatives of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But you stated that you prepared yourself for the testimony here.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you prepared yourself?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I wrote down these names so that I wouldn't go through an extreme effort of trying to recollect them here, because my brain is tired as it is. And while they asked questions back there, I had time to come up with an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you give them names during those interviews?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you read your statement at the end, read and sign every page of your statement?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to read out a segment of your statement of 2nd June of 1999 which was given by you to the investigators of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Has it got a paragraph number, Mr. Vasic, so the translators can pick it up?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That's document ID 224A. It's in B/C/S language, on page 3, paragraph 4. It starts with the name Savo Todovic. "Savo Todovic was his deputy and I saw him often in the camp. I did not know him from before. Other detainees told me that he worked in KP Dom even before the war. I only spoke to him once. I went to the factory because I wanted to work. Todovic told me that I couldn't work due to my handicap. He was in charge of everything. He seemed to me to be more responsible than Krnojelac, who in my opinion was the warden only on paper." Did you state this?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Is it true?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Well, this was a figure of speech. Krnojelac cannot be less responsible. I simply said it there figuratively speaking. Krnojelac was the warden and this other man was his deputy, and so in this general context, this is how I came to give this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You stated here that, based on your opinion, Mr. Krnojelac was only the warden on paper. Is it true that you stated that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, but simply -- if I may add, I said it. It is true that I said it, but he was the warden. Now, it is quite insignificant that I made a comparison between the two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Sir, you gave this statement. Based on your own words, you gave this to the best of your recollection and ability, and you gave the statement voluntarily. Now, were you saying the truth at the time?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I was not saying the truth because he was not insignificant. I assessed them based on what was happening in the camp because he was not really showing up frequently, whereas his deputy was. And I'm not saying this to justify him and I'm not saying this to add to his liability because it is a well-known fact what was done by Krnojelac and what was done by Todovic, so each man should be held accountable for what they did. I as a handicapped person spent 820 days in a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Sir, so did you just tell me that you were not saying the truth to the investigator of the Prosecution on the 2nd of June, 1999, despite the fact that you had stated that you would give the statement to the best of your ability, voluntarily, and that after that you had signed the statement as an accurate statement?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: The word that I used is really a tiniest fraction of what happened to me during those 820 days, so you can basically disregard it. I cannot relieve him of his responsibility through that statement of mine, and I cannot add to his liability, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I did not ask you to release him or to add to his liability, I simply asked you whether you had stated this and whether this was true. Did you indeed give the statement to the investigator? You said you did. Now I asked you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, he has said now three times. That is what he said. He sought to explain it away. Don't you think that you may have made enough of this? It's a question really for us at the end, not for the witness. He has maintained throughout he was in fact the warden. Now, if he was in fact the warden and we hold him responsible for what Mr. Todovic did, that's another matter, but you're not going to get anywhere by arguing with the witness. You've got his statement; he had said what you read out to him. It's up to us to make what we can of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you say to the investigator of the Prosecution, did you also state that Mr. Sekulovic, upon arriving in July of 1993, stated that if military police were to come and look for any of you, that he had no authority to stop them, to prevent them?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you, in the same statement to the investigator, say that you infrequently saw Mr. Krnojelac at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you -- were you a member of SDA in 1992?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When asked by my learned colleague, you stated that you were in possession of a weapon.

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What kind of a weapon did you have?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: A revolver, pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was that the only weapon you had?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: I also had a grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you also have a German rifle, Schmeisser?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: We had it as one of our weapons, but it was not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you state to the investigators of the Prosecution that you paid 1200 German marks for a German rifle Schmeisser, and that it was purchased by your brother, and another one?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you, prior to being arrested, have in your possession this rifle?

utterances.speaker: AHMET HADZIMUSIC
utterances.text: Occasionally I had it in my possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, but it is 4.00, and I don't know if this would be an appropriate time to stop cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's a strange clock this, because each side seems to see it from a different perspective but still manage to finish some minutes early. However, we'll adjourn now until 9.30 tomorrow.
